newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD auction suspended mid-bid.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD auction suspended mid-bid.

text.p: Latin America's largest privatisation was dramatically halted midway through the bidding Tuesday when a court official charged onto Rio de Janeiro's stock exchange floor with a court injunction in hand.

Officials of Brazil's National Development Bank, which runs the country's privatisation programme and was overseeing the sell-off of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), said they expected to quash the court order soon and resume the auction.
"We should be able to have the injunction overturned today and continue the auction today," said Tereza Cristina Aquino, the development bank's privatisation superintendent.

The abrupt halt to the sale, which occured just as the bidding reached a 13.2 percent premium over the 26.67 reais (about $25) per share base price, extended a week-long battle between government lawyers and courts across the country.

Originally scheduled for April 29, the sell-off of up to 45 percent of the voting shares of the world's largest iron ore exporter finally began Tuesday at midday after the government managed to quash a host of injunctions.
"It's a pity," President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said of Tuesday's latest setback during a visit to neighbouring Uruguay, according to news agencies Invest News and Agencia Estado.
Outside the Rio de Janeiro bolsa where the auction was taking place, police set attack dogs on demonstrators who were throwing rocks and chanting abuse.

Local authorities said four policemen and two protesters were injured in the clashes, which were on a much smaller scale than the ferocious battles which took place on the original April 29 auction date.
Brazil hopes to raise some $5 billion with the privatisation of the jewel in its public sector crown, making the sell-off Latin America's biggest to date.

The process has been fraught with controversy, with opponents ranging from former presidents to Catholic bishops as well as leftists accusing Brasilia of selling off the country's mineral wealth for a pittance.
The government's plans generated an avalanche of more than 120 lawsuits, most of them filed at the last minute in what officials have called "guerrilla warfare."

The court order that suspended the auction Tuesday was granted by a Rio de Janeiro regional court at the request of a group of employees of CVRD, a massive concern which owns ports, railways and mines iron ore, gold and bauxite, among others.
It was carried dramatically onto the bolsa floor by a striding court official, who was immediately swamped by a dozen television camera crews, stock exchange security guards and auction officials.
